2) Immediate asks from your side: site inventory (owned by TheraGene), acceptable maintenance windows, and any internal SOC2/IT evidence we can reference.

3) Proposed Redwood actions: markus to coordinate an initial HW compatibility gap analysis with engineering; ava to share offline install MOP and sample network diagram; Priyom to draft a mutual action plan (MAP) with key milestones and procurement checklist.

Markus — initial MOP outline and checklist below (high level). I’ll produce a full doc by 1/22 for the gap analysis.

MOP outline (short):
- Pre-deploy: verify inventory + serials, validate hardware firmware versions against supported list, collect HBA/NIC driver versions, snapshot current GPU firmware and record checksums.
- Installer staging: signed installer bundle (SHA256) placed on jumpbox; TheraGene to transfer to isolated staging host; offline validation kit runs smoke tests (model load, kv cache warmup, canned prompts).
- Upgrade window: schedule 4-hour maintenance window per rack; apply firmware updates in staggered 1-rack batches, validate models load and latency targets, if failure revert using snapshot images.
- Logging & evidence: collect system logs, Redwood runtime trace, KV cache snapshot, and signed validation report; provide audit package to TheraGene for regulatory retention.

Required artifacts from TheraGene: staging host access procedure, signing key fingerprint for jumpbox transfers, preferred maintenance windows.

I’ll include a fallback plan (hosted fallback / temporary dedicated burst) in the full analysis in case a rollback cannot be completed in the window.

-Marissa

Summary of findings (excerpt):
- Compatibility: 90% of listed servers are supported; two older GPU models (RTX A5000 gen1) will require firmware upgrade prior to install — this will need a 1-rack maintenance window and a rollback image.
- Offline validation path: proposed validation kit runs locally and generates a signed report; final signature verification can be performed by TheraGene KMS or Redwood-offline tool.
- Risk: if jumpbox transfer is limited to weekly windows, initial model bootstrap could take 48–72 hours; recommend staging model cache on a portable NVMe image to reduce net staging time.
